target.role: fresh whole-journey belonging and placement discovery for STRANGE GAIT
target.position: Whole journey: before the opener, between every non-protected pair, or after the tail. Preserve only Transparency → When We Froze and When We Froze → Stardancer; Truth in Noise → Transparency remains available.
target.purpose: Test one current structural transformation and four unused adjacent or overlooked exact-track hypotheses. Character changes are allowed; admission still requires purposeful transition, local-run and long-form effect.

sourceWindows: CURRENT / MUSICRADAR: https://www.musicradar.com/artists/as-soon-as-i-started-writing-music-with-computers-i-got-so-addicted-to-it-tom-vr-on-his-creative-process-game-changing-ableton-live-tips-and-the-hardware-synth-he-cant-stop-talking-about — the August 18, 2026 studio feature and September 15 release window were screened. The title track was retained because the artist and writer document a complete 4/4-to-broken internal transformation.

CURRENT / WEEKLY AND ALBUM WINDOWS: https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/sep/04/add-to-playlist-the-churning-darkness-of-barcelona-producer-nueen-and-the-weeks-best-new-tracks and https://pitchfork.com/story/9-new-albums-you-should-listen-to-now-chat-pile-melissa-auf-der-maur-and-more — September 4, 2026 release coverage was screened; genre-adjacent identities without exact-track techno or structural evidence stayed below the ranked list.

ADJACENT / PLANET MU: https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/rian-treanor-ataxia — ATAXIA's ten-track window was screened. Rian Treanor — ATAXIA B1 was retained from the exact polyrhythmic build account.

ADJACENT / PEAK OIL: https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/wrecked-lightship-antiposition — Antiposition's six-track window was screened. Wrecked Lightship — Sunken Skies was retained from the exact quick-stepping-dub-to-stuttering-breakbeats transformation.

ADJACENT / I.O.T RECORDS: https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/azu-tiwaline-draw-me-a-silence — Draw Me a Silence's twelve-track window was screened. Azu Tiwaline — Luz Azul was retained from its exact resonant-texture and syncopated-beat description.

OVERLOOKED CATALOGUE / WARP: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clark_(album) — Clark's thirteen-track album window and cited review descriptions were screened. Clark — Banjo was retained from the exact Detroit-electro and chaotic-beat-manipulation account.

ADDITIONAL WINDOWS: Skee Mask's 808BB, T++'s Wireless and Audio1995#8, Helena Hauff's Actio Reactio, Wrecked Lightship's neighbouring tracks, current 2026 electronic roundups and legacy Resident Advisor/Pitchfork rhythmic searches were screened. Removed Spotify catalogue, identity-only results, release-level claims and tracks already retained in STRANGE GAIT stayed below the ranked list.
explorationReceipt.approximateInspectedScope: Approximately 46 named tracks and releases across current releases, adjacent and emerging artists and labels, and overlooked catalogue windows; metadata and attributed descriptions only, with zero audio auditions.
exclusions: All 14 canonical identities, active placement-specific rejects and every untriggered PARKED revisit were excluded. Exact identities and primary discovery lanes retained in Runs 53–80 were not recycled.
The protected internal handoffs Transparency → When We Froze and When We Froze → Stardancer remain unavailable; Truth in Noise → Transparency and every other boundary remain available.
No lead was promoted for recency, reputation, genre, novelty, title or technical cleverness. Current-release pages without exact-track rhythmic or structural evidence were scan context only.

Energy, density, space, hypnosis, emotional effect, phrase structure, harmonic relation, perceived pulse and mixability remain unknown. Attributed descriptions of rhythm and transformation are evidence, not transition or flow verdicts.
rankedLeadSummary: 1. Tom VR — Don't Know How Fast I'm Moving Until I Hit Something: strongest current exact-track internal transformation, documented by the artist and studio feature.
2. Rian Treanor — ATAXIA B1: strongest explicit polyrhythmic build from an overlooked experimental-techno album.
3. Wrecked Lightship — Sunken Skies: strongest quick-stepping dub to stuttering-breakbeats transformation from an adjacent bass/techno world.
4. Azu Tiwaline — Luz Azul: strongest syncopated-percussion lead from a body/head bass-techno intersection.
5. Clark — Banjo: strongest overlooked electro/techno lead with exact chaotic beat manipulation.
